speaker: clrirmarkbennett
text: Hunter's Hill Day, celebrated each year on July 31, is an opportunity to bring the community together to celebrate the location in which we are fortunate to live and build our connections with each other.

speaker: markbennett
text: This year, July 31 celebrations have been impacted by the spread of COVID-19 throughout Australia and around the world. This year, the number of visitors to Hunter's Hill Day has increased by more than 1,000. celebrated each year on July 31 is an opportunity to bring the community together to celebrate the location in which we are fortunate to live and build our connections with each other. This year, July 31 celebrations have been impacted by the spread of COVID-19 throughout the world and we will be celebrating in a different way. Further, many events in our annual calendar have been cancelled or postponed, which has been necessary but very disappointing. Currently in our municipality, there is a strong sense of community built on shared

speaker: clrirmarkbennett
text: values, shared history and the shared challenges we face together. Our social networks remain strong with our clubs, volunteer groups, churches, meeting places and community groups all making very important contributions to our lifestyle. text: each other face-to-face will be an added challenge. Building a stronger community will rely on our awareness and our ability to build community connections deliberately, not accidentally. text: Good evening, Mr Mayor and Councillors and Hunters Hill staff or personnel. Thanks for the opportunity to present tonight. What I want to talk tonight about is the impact of the bottleneck into the estate. I'm a civil engineer, a chartered professional engineer and a fellow of Engineers Australia. I've spent my whole career building motorways and road infrastructure around Australia. So it's a very passionate item I'd like to talk to. There should be a presentation that— Councillor interjecting. Councillor GRIFFITHS.

speaker: mikezambelli

So, what I'd like to talk tonight about is, from the previous meeting with the Council, item 1 that was documented, it was agreed to put a no parking sign on the southern side of St Malo, which is the entrance into Portbough Point. What I want to talk tonight about is removing that time restriction of 7am to 5pm Monday to Friday, and just making it a blank no parking sign. Next slide. A number of reasons that a lot of residents in the estate believe we need an unrestricted parking zone, I've highlighted there. Some of the key ones, the first one there, St Malo Avenue is the entrance into the property, and by having cars parked on both sides, it's a very tight bottleneck, and I've got a couple of photos just to show the effect of that. What essentially we now have is a one-way restricted entrance into the estate, outside those hours, because of parking on both sides, and I'm very concerned at the safety risk that that's presenting to traffic and pedestrians around the area. We also have a lot of traffic outside the 7pm to 5pm. Me, myself, when I come home from work, it's after 5pm, and I leave home before 7am in the morning, as do a lot of residents to get to work. So, that's why I think the 7pm to 5pm time restraint isn't quite what we need. The waste collection trucks that come into the estate, they come in at 6am in the morning, and I've been told by some residents that they actually have to honk their horns to allow cars to get out of the way so they can physically fit through the bottleneck, and you'll see what I mean from the photos that we're about to look at. I've also been told by other residents that heavy vehicles, whether they're semis, loaded trucks, etc., concrete agitators, when they're coming in for renovations, etc., they actually have to swerve into some of the driveways on the northern side to get around the cars that park on the southern side, and we are only talking about four cars, car parking of four cars, that's restricting the whole estate. Next slide. What I've shown there, the green boundary is essentially all the residents that are affected by this bottleneck. There's 134 homes that have access into Pulpit Point. You can see the marina top right. There's tennis courts, two swimming pools, community centre. On a weekend, we get a lot of people coming into the marina. They have functions down in the community centre, weddings, kids' parties, all those type of things. On a weekend, it's quite an active estate, and that's, again, why this time restriction just isn't really satisfactory for what we're after. There's a lot of renovations going on. I'm in a strata of 11 units. Three out of the 11 units at the moment are actually going through renovations, so there's continual flow of trucks in and out of the estate during the week, early mornings, after hours, etc. So this car parking on the southern side, which I've shown there by that red arrow, it really just restricts the whole access into the estate, and it's just a matter of time until we have a number of vehicle damage or incidents occurring in the estate. Next slide. If anyone's got any questions, just feel free to pull me up.

The left-hand photo shows a car coming down the street, but the two on the side with the blue utility, you can see on the far right photo, you've got a couple of hundred mil between the cars parked and cars coming down the street. This is the main entrance for 134 homes, and on the right-hand side, what we're talking about is car parking for four cars that's constraining the whole estate. Next page. I believe there's been an objection from one of the residents on the southern side. There's only a couple of residents that have driveway access on that side, and I believe that the objection was they wanted to be able to allow an elderly person to park on the side of the road and come into their property. They actually have a five-metre driveway, and the photo on the left there shows how large the driveway is. You can park four cars in there. There is really no reason to have car parking just to allow—or to accommodate the objection that's come from this resident. There is enough room in that driveway to get someone in, and even with an unrestricted no parking sign, they still have five minutes to allow that elderly person to get out of their car and get into their front gate, just shown in that bottom photo. As you probably know, a no parking sign even allows anyone to park and have two-minute access to get out of their car. Just in wrapping up, my belief is there's a real safety issue with this bottleneck into the community. A lot of us have been putting up with it for some time. Just as a matter of fact, St Malo Avenue is extremely narrow when you look at Waibelina Road just around the corner that allows for parking on both sides. It's metres wider, and we just don't have that width to accommodate parking on the southern side. So, my request is if Council can please reconsider putting a time constraint, and we just have a standard no parking zone sign on that southern side of St Malo for the entrance into the estate. Thank you.

speaker: rosswilliams
text: Yes, Mr Mayor. I've attended several of the local government conferences, either at a federal or at a state level, and I think they're a very critical part of local government. They're a part of where local government as a whole develops the industry and develops its role with its community, and also identifies where advocacy needs to be done on behalf of local government. And I think it is a very important role that Huntersville should be present at that, and should take whatever opportunities it has to participate in the voting process. And we have two delegates available, one the Mayor and obviously now the Deputy Mayor, and I think if either of those are unable to attend, then we should have a fallback position for somebody who is going to attend anyway, to be involved, to make engagement with the motion process, which is a very critical part of the conference. So, I'm a strong believer in local government having the opportunity to develop the industry collectively, to form views and take on board the views of individual councils, to make sure that local government is representative, and that issues that the Local Government Association or New South Wales Local Government pursue as their priorities reflected in what the priorities of local government collectively believe in. So, I think it's vital that we have adequate voting delegates, and as I say, I'll be attending in any case. And I will be going with the limit of $1,000, and I'm quite prepared to pay for the rest myself, as I have done in the past. So, Mr. Mayor, I commend the opportunity for Council to, as a whole, to participate in the process. So, I look forward to the conference, and I think it's very beneficial to this council and to local government as a whole.
